q1_whyAreWidthBandsFrozen.answer: Because the clone's CSS makes exactly ONE width-dependent decision and everything else is a pixel snapshot. Two subtrees ship in one document (.wr-variant data-wr-viewport desktop|mobile, runtime-template.ts:313-346); a single inferred breakpoint of 915 = floor((390+1440)/2) (responsive-plan.ts:74-81) switches between them via (max-width: 914.98px) / (min-width: 915px) (app-template.ts:298-308). Inside each subtree every box carries the computed style resolved at ONE observation width — 1440 for desktop, 390 for mobile — emitted verbatim as px including width/min-width/max-width and resolved grid-template-columns; only <html>/<body> are exempted (style-generator.ts:115-122). The single escape hatch, the recovered fluid tier, is desktop-only (the selector hardcodes data-wr-viewport="desktop" at layout-inference.ts:701), needs >= 2 desktop probe samples including 1440 (:323-329), needs BLOCKISH_DISPLAY (:388-391) and refuses grid items and basis-governed flex items (:230-289). So 0..914.98 is 100% frozen at 390 values and 915..infinity is frozen at 1440 values except for the minority of nodes that clear that funnel. There is no continuous reflow mechanism, only a two-position switch.

The source's real switch is 1025 (@media (max-width:1024px){.hide-laptop{display:none!important}} paired with @media (min-width:1025px){.show-laptop{display:none!important}}), so across 1025..1231.98 the clone hides what the source shows. Two further facts matter: (a) the band's LOWER edge is wrong in the opposite direction — because 1024 is the first desktop sample, line 674's `previous ? midpoint : entry.width` pins the start to 1024 exactly, so across 915..1023.98 the clone SHOWS the table the source hides; both edges must move, not just the upper one; (b) the band is not the only defect at 1100 — even with it removed, the desktop subtree's 1440-pinned px clips content (I measured 250 offscreen chars and 174 overflowing nodes in the shipped build at 1100).

q4_whatDoesTheSourceActuallyDo.answer: linear.app's responsiveness is 100% declarative CSS with zero runtime dependency. The /pricing comparison table pivots on ONE desktop-first breakpoint: @media (max-width:1024px) hides the 5-column header row via the generic utility ([data-hide="laptop"], .hide-laptop { display:none !important }) and reshapes .PDOlRq_row to flex; @media (min-width:1025px) hides the complementary mobile plan picker. Above 1024 the row's UNCONDITIONAL base rule is `grid-template-columns: 2fr repeat(4,1fr); display:grid` — fluid fr, resolving to '448px 224px x4' at 1440 and '360px 180px x4' at 1100. Same rule, different pixels: that is why the source is correct at 1100 with no extra breakpoint. Site-wide there are 381 media rules across 81 sheets (436 KB), of which 226 are width-conditioned (26 KB); design-system breakpoints are 640/768/1024/1280; 6 media-conditioned :root token rules (461 bytes) carry --homepage-padding-inset / --homepage-outer-padding / --header-height / --grid-columns / --page-padding-y; 10 hide/show utilities (968 bytes) drive EVERY desktop/mobile DOM swap on the site. Container queries exist but only in a video player and a chart axis — not on any page layout. Not one width-based matchMedia call, 0 ResizeObservers, and element count is exactly 3,246 at every width: nothing is conditionally rendered, both parallel subtrees coexist permanently. With JS disabled the table behaves identically at all five widths, and even the mobile plan switcher still works because it is :has(option[value=X]:checked).

q6_doesAdditionalObservationAloneSolveIt.answer: NO — and the experiment is decisive. Strategy A re-observed /pricing with probeExtraWidths [700,1100] (7 widths, 0 node drift at the truth width) and spliced the arrays into a SiteSpec copy, isolating extra samples as the only variable. Every measured field at every width came back IDENTICAL to C1, a ten-line band clamp: 1024 still BLOCKER, 1100 still BLOCKER (band now correct, but revealing the table pushes MORE content offscreen — 362 unreachable chars vs 250 before), 700 bit-identical to baseline. The reason is structural: the geometry tier is gated by containing-block guards, BLOCKISH_DISPLAY and the parent-probe requirement, not by sample count, so extra samples change exactly one thing — the interpolated hidden band. HOWEVER, one extra sample is INDISPENSABLE as an input to the correction that does work: fluidity detection needs two probe widths both above the site's top authored switch, and on linear the shipped pair (1440,1920) finds 9 fluid nodes of 1,264 because the layout caps near 1440, while adding a single 1100 sample finds 508. So: more observation alone buys nothing; one well-chosen extra sample is load-bearing for the fix that works.

The mechanism works: 81 sheets fetched past the CORS trap, 3,531 rules parsed, 621 kept, 220 emitted after translating every selector to [data-wr-node] by rebuilding the observed DOM offline and mapping sourceElementId -> nodeId — 0 unmatched selectors, 0 unsupported selectors. The RESULT is worse than baseline: 1440 REGRESSED from exact (2,461 chars) to 2,543 because preserving only LAYOUT properties lets both .hide-laptop and .show-laptop paint; 1100 produced the worst visual of the three (duplicated stacked CTAs, plan cards colliding with the trusted-by strip) because preserved fluid rules override only the handful of properties they declare while ~5.9k surrounding nodes keep 1440-resolved px; 1024 and 1100 both stayed BLOCKER. To be correct it would need the FULL cascade (visibility, content, pseudo-elements) plus @layer replay — materially more, not less — and structurally it needs (a) source class/data-* identity persisted through the SiteSpec, which today is emptied to {} (I verified 0 occurrences in the served clone), and (b) build-time fetch of the LIVE source stylesheets, surrendering the asset independence Task 22 established.

q11_canWeMeetTheFiveRequiredWidths.answer: YES as FIVE VERIFIED WIDTHS; NO as continuous responsive equivalence; and not yet with anything tested. The architecture and the requirement are compatible in principle: the clone is a discrete band switch, the user asked for five discrete widths, and nothing about that requires implementing a CSS layout engine — it requires only that each named width lands in a band whose styles were MEASURED (or provably fluid) at that width, and that each width is RENDERED and compared rather than inferred. Concretely: (i) 1024 and 1100 are already demonstrably reachable — I measured AC5 at offscreenTextChars 0 / overflowing 0 and 12 respectively; (ii) 390 and 1440 are already exact in the shipped build and must be treated as regression-protected, which is precisely where AC5 currently fails; (iii) 700 is the one required width no strategy has moved, and its fix is identified but UNTESTED — run the inference for the mobile subtree too by lifting the hardcoded data-wr-viewport="desktop" at layout-inference.ts:701 and using the probe widths BELOW the breakpoint, which needs a ~700 sample the way the desktop side needed 1100; (iv) the newly-exposed defect class (lost flex justification / row gaps) must be fixed, since it is currently the price of every gain and it lands at 1440 too. What is NOT realistically available on this architecture is arbitrary-width fidelity: every width between samples remains interpolation, and the responsive-hidden tier still ships unverified because the only truth render is at 1440 — so the truth check must gain in-band render widths, otherwise 'five widths' is still five guesses. The honest deliverable is 'verified at 390/700/1024/1100/1440', explicitly not 'responsive'.

That information is thrown away TWICE. First at capture, by the CORS trap: the observer walks document.styleSheets and 30 of 81 sheets throw, and they are the load-bearing ones. I verified the consequence in the IR myself: authoredLayout on 34 of 3,254 nodes on /pricing, and the ONLY media condition anywhere is (max-width: 640px). The 1024 breakpoint governing the entire table is simply absent. Reproduced on a second site (stripe: 0 of 8 readable, authoredLayout on 0 of 2,280 elements).

Second by an explicit design decision: layout-inference.ts:463 and :541 are the only two consumers of authoredLayout[].media and both use `rule.media === undefined` to EXCLUDE media-conditioned declarations, demoting what survives into provenance prose. Zero authored responsive semantics reach generated CSS by construction.

Inference then invents what it was never told: a boundary 207px off the truth, shipped 738 times, 503 of them on one page. Preserved information would have snapped that edge to a measured 1025 instead of a guessed 1232.

The winning mechanism's ONE external input — which two probe widths to compare — is exactly a preserved-source fact (the site's top authored layout switch: 1024 on linear, 940 on stripe). Agent E showed it cannot be recovered from the IR. Without preservation, the best available fix is un-parameterizable and has to be hand-tuned per site.
evidenceAgainst: Strategy B is a direct, measured refutation of 'preserve → emit'. Preserving real source rules and replaying them produced the WORST result of the three and REGRESSED 1440, the one width that was exact.

The reason is structural, not a bug in B: preservation is not composable with a frozen exact-computed tier. A partial subset (layout properties only) lets both halves of a hide/show utility pair paint; the full cascade would be needed, plus @layer replay, which B bypassed with !important and could therefore not cleanly re-cascade.

The clone has already destroyed the identity preserved rules need — I verified 0 occurrences of the source's classes and data-* attributes in the served HTML — so 'preserve' at the CSS layer implies a second preservation programme at the DOM layer.

And 'preserve' at build time means fetching the LIVE source origin, surrendering the asset independence Task 22 established and making builds non-reproducible against a site that has since redeployed.

adoptedFormulation.capture: PRESERVE — fetch every stylesheet by <link href> (never trust in-page cssRules) and record authored width-conditioned rules, condition text and authored fluid values into the IR. This is the single highest-value change identified in 28.5C and it is independent of every strategy.
adoptedFormulation.ir: PRESERVE — carry authored breakpoint numbers and authored fluid declarations as first-class IR facts, not as evidence prose. Stop excluding media-conditioned declarations with `rule.media === undefined`.
adoptedFormulation.observe: OBSERVE — choose probe widths FROM the preserved breakpoint histogram so at least two samples sit strictly inside each authored band, instead of a hardcoded global grid.
adoptedFormulation.infer: INFER — keep ONE generated CSS tier, but let preserved facts CONSTRAIN it: snap band edges to authored breakpoints instead of midpoints; prefer an authored fr/%/clamp value over a resolved px when the probe already proves the node fluid; refuse rather than extrapolate where no authored fact and no bracketing sample exist.
adoptedFormulation.verify: VERIFY — the missing fourth clause the evidence demands. The one rule kind that ships without a render (responsive-hidden: 738 rules, all acceptedUnchecked, verified in the manifest) is exactly the kind that shipped a 207px error to release. Any width the product promises must be rendered and compared, not inferred.

principleAdjudication.netAdjudication: The evidence supports adopting the principle for WHERE INFORMATION IS ACQUIRED AND STORED, and refutes it for HOW CSS IS EMITTED. 'Preserve → emit verbatim' is measurably worse than what we ship today. 'Preserve → inform inference → verify by render' is supported by every strand of evidence in the task, including the strand that killed Strategy B.

verdict: RESPONSIVE ROOT CAUSE KNOWN — MORE EXPERIMENT NEEDED

verdictRationale.whyNotSimpleFixReadyToImplement: The candidate is not shippable as-is and I confirmed the reason from the pixels, not from a report. BLOCKER=0 at five widths is real but METRIC-RELATIVE: the clip metric that produced it reads 0 offscreen chars at 1440 for BOTH the shipped build and AC5, while AC5's nav has collapsed ~280px out of position there ('Sign up' right edge 1361 -> 1081, verified live and in a native-resolution crop). Shipping it would trade two BLOCKER widths for a systemic MAJOR-class regression at a width that is currently faithful, with one shared unexplained signature (lost flex justification and row gaps) that nobody has root-caused. Two further gaps are load-bearing: 700 — a REQUIRED width and the largest single fidelity gap in the set — is byte-untouched by every strategy and its fix is identified but never run; and the mechanism's probe-pair input cannot be read from the IR at all, so it is not yet parameterizable per site. Stripe generalized only after a correction that linear's probe pair happened to mask, which is itself evidence that one more site can still surface a new mandatory correction.
verdictRationale.whyNotArchitectureRequiresRedesign: The root cause is fully identified, localized and reproducible: one function (hiddenRanges, layout-inference.ts:661-684), one constant (LAYOUT_PROBE_WIDTHS, observer/types.ts:1103), one hardcoded selector (:701), one filter (:323-327) and one verification hole (layout-truth-check.ts:107). A ~55-line change in a single file, with no schema change, no new runtime dependency and no loss of source independence, already converted both broken widths from structurally-broken to structurally-correct, and ran unmodified on a second, unrelated site. Nothing in the evidence shows the two-subtree band architecture must be replaced; it shows that frozen-px emission and one interpolation function are wrong, and that a capture bug starves the whole thing of the facts it needs. Calling for redesign here would discard a working, cheap, generalizing direction.
verdictRationale.whyMoreExperimentIsExactlyRight: Three questions remain open and each is an experiment, not an implementation detail: (1) WHAT is the lost-flex-justification/row-gap defect class? It is introduced by the unfreeze wherever it acts, including at 1440; the audit believes the logo row, the header bar, the wrapped rows and the collapsed toggle are ONE fix, and that hypothesis has never been tested. Until it is, every gain carries a regression. (2) DOES the mobile-subtree fix work? Lifting the desktop-only selector at :701 and running inference below the breakpoint is the identified production fix for 700; it has not been emulated once. (3) CAN the probe pair and band edges be driven by preserved authored breakpoints instead of hand-picked widths? That needs the CORS-trap capture fix first, and it is the difference between a per-site tuning exercise and a general mechanism. All three are cheap to answer with exactly the disposable-app method 28.5C already established, and answering them converts this into a genuinely simple implementation task.

dissents.claim: 'The table's 1100px failure in the reconstruction is therefore not a missing breakpoint — it is a baked fixed-px substitution for a fluid fr-based grid.'
dissents.myPosition: WRONG AS STATED about the clone, and dangerously so. I verified live that at 1100 in the shipped build the header row n000357 is display:none by its OWN synthesized band rule with all five column labels unreachable and visibleChars 2348 vs 2672 — the columns are ABSENT, not clipped. Agent C is describing the SOURCE's rule set (where 1100 and 1440 genuinely share rules) and generalizing it to the clone, where a synthetic band the source does not have is the proximate cause. Both causes are real and orthogonal — Agent B has this right. An implementer following C's framing would go straight past the 738-block band.

Right about the source, wrong about the pipeline. An extra sample strictly inside the source's top band is precisely what raises fluid-node detection from 9 to 508 on linear, and the winning variant's shipped band edge (1061.98 = midpoint(1024,1100)) proves it consumed that sample. C and D disagree here; D is correct. The defensible version of C's point is narrower: extra widths alone fix nothing (Strategy A proved that), but one well-chosen extra width is a required input.

dissents.claim: 'Every load-bearing selector would still match. Nothing in the capture blocks this approach.'
dissents.myPosition: False for the shipped clone, and I verified it: 0 occurrences of PDOlRq / data-plan / data-header-row / hide-laptop in the served /pricing HTML, versus 429 / 228 / 2 / 3 in the observation dom.json. Agent D caught this; it should be carried forward loudly, because it is a large part of why Strategy B is expensive.
